Step 1: Secure same job, same pay rights for labour hire workers.
Step 2: Bring these labour hire workers back in house.
We are incredibly disappointed by the announcement of staff redundancies at CIT. It's not fair on our members, it's not fair on workers and it isn't fair on students.

Interim pay increases have been announced for non-APS agencies with agreements that expire before the 28th of February 2027. If your agency is affected, you will have received an email from us with more details.

The Coalition took a plan to slash 41,000 public sector jobs to the last election and were thrashed. According to Einstein, the definition of insanity is doing the same thing over again and expecting different results. Who knows, maybe Angus is smarter than Albert. What we do know is that it doesn't matter who's leading the Liberal Party, they keep coming back to the same old failed policies.

Private employment service providers do not serve the public good - their only motive is to make as much money as possible. For-profit companies should never have been trusted with the task of supporting jobseekers.

Apparently CSIRO boss Doug Hinton feels uncomfortable getting a $140k bonus at the same time as he's cutting 1100 jobs. Not uncomfortable enough to pay it back or donate it to a worthy cause, but you know...

Do you think it's fair? 

Private labour hire companies hold contracts in the hundreds of millions in Australia.

Workers hired through these companies are doing ATO work, directed by the ATO, on ATO systems - but are paid 40% less than directly employed ATO staff.

And in worse working conditions to boot.

That's why the CPSU have made a submission to the landmark 'Same Job Same Pay' case. This arrangement is unfair for the labour hire workers, the ATO workers, and the taxpayer.

The only people that benefit from the current employment system are the private, for-profit corporations. These massive companies prioritise money over finding appropriate, meaningful employment for jobseekers. It is time for the government to bring the employment system back into public hands - for the good of jobseekers, businesses, taxpayers, and most importantly, workers.

The ACT government's latest pay offer is not up to scratch. 66% of CPSU members voted to reject the deal, and we will be running a Vote NO campaign until the government improves the offer.

CPSU members and delegates would like to thank ACTU leaders Sally McManus and Michele O’Neil for their tireless efforts leading the Australian union movement over much of the past decade. 

They were the first all-female leadership team in the ACTU’s 99-year history. Under their direction, union membership is growing and wages are increasing. 

They also successfully campaigned for the right to disconnect law, same job, same pay protections, wage theft criminalisation and ensuring minimum pay, insurance and safety standards for gig economy workers. 

Both Sally and Michele were great friends and allies of the CPSU lending their support to many of our campaigns including Working From Home, outsourcing, opposing public sector job cuts, CSL bargaining and protecting the CSIRO. 

And while there are many challenges ahead for working Australians, these two unionists are leaving the movement in a strong and united position. 

CPSU members congratulate them of their many achievements and wish them well for their future endeavours. 

@ausunions Sally McManus @micheleoneilau

The Government says public services should be delivered by public sector workers. So why is the ATO still lining the pockets of labour hire companies for work its own staff can do? It’s time to bring these jobs back in-house.
